_comment: Recording of live run 42 (status partial); the plan is the model's own words.

steps.message: Reviewing the intake and the question.

claims.text: The goal is a 30% cut in electricity bought from the grid by 2030, on a $400,000 capital budget. Efficiency alone is estimated to cut grid use by about 6% to 18%, which is roughly 21% to 59% of the way to the goal. It does not reach the goal.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The efficiency package is estimated to cost about $39,800 to $136,600 upfront, well inside the $400,000 budget. Meeting the 30% goal is likely to need measures beyond this standard package, and those were not costed in this run.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: A new rooftop solar array is not an option on the current roof plan. The existing 380 kW array already fills the usable roof, so no free roof remains. Solar scenarios B and C could not be costed.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: The heating fuel appears to be natural gas, which an electricity-use goal does not cover. Heating was not part of this plan.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: P.S. 24 (X024), an elementary school at 660 West 236th Street, the Bronx. Built 1953, flat roof, Con Edison customer. Floor area 115,325 sq ft and roof area 40,500 sq ft as entered by the user.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Annual grid electricity of 226,605 kWh (energy over time) matches the city's Local Law 84 energy report for 2024 and is treated as measured. The baseline for the goal is the electricity the building buys from the grid; the existing solar already lowers it.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Existing systems taken into account: a solar array already on the roof, entered by the user as 380 kW (how much power at one moment). The user listed no other existing renewables and no existing efficiency work, so the plan assumes none.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city's tax record shows a gross floor area of 135,600 sq ft, against 115,325 sq ft entered by the user. The city's energy report also uses 115,325 sq ft. The user's figure is kept as the working number; please confirm it.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city's address for this lot is 660 West 235th Street, while the address asked for was 660 West 236th Street. It may be another frontage of the same lot.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city's building outlines for the lot total about 40,497 sq ft across two buildings, close to the 40,500 sq ft roof area entered. An outline is ground area, not a measured roof, so the roof area still needs checking by an engineer or roofer.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The owning agency is the Department of Education (DOE). The city's tax record shows no landmark flag.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Usable roof setback factor of 0.55 (share of the roof left after edges, equipment and access paths).
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Array density of 66 sq ft of roof per kW of panels.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Efficiency measures (LED and controls) save 10-20% of annual use. This is a planning estimate, not a cited benchmark and not a building model.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Planning-level benchmark prices, not quotes: efficiency cost per kWh saved per year $1.17-4.02 (standard), from the middle half of completed NYC public-sector projects since 2016 (NYSERDA data). Standard efficiency saving 10-20%, deep 15-25%; these savings percents are planning estimates, but only 62%-88% of them is counted because the City's audited projects delivered that share (NYC DCAS Local Law 87 report FY2022).
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: The city's 2024 energy report shows a site EUI (energy use per square foot) of 48.4 kBtu (thousand BTU) per sq ft and an ENERGY STAR score of 93. Reported natural gas use is about 4.35 million kBtu, so heating is not electric and sits outside an electricity goal.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: A standard efficiency package (LED lighting and controls) is estimated to save about 14,050 to 39,882 kWh a year, or 6.2% to 17.6% of grid use. Only 62% to 88% of the predicted savings is counted, because the City's audited projects delivered that share. The trimmed percent is not added back.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The intake says no efficiency work has been done and does not say what lighting is installed. The plan assumes none. If lighting is already LED, the savings and their confidence are lower. Please confirm lighting type, controls and cooling type.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Annual savings from the efficiency package are estimated at about $2,800 to $9,600, using the New York commercial average price of 19.8 to 24.2 cents per kWh, not this building's own tariff.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: A roof of 40,500 sq ft with a 0.55 setback leaves about 22,275 sq ft usable, which fits about 337.5 kW of panels at 66 sq ft per kW.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The solar production tool declined to size a new array: the existing 380 kW array already uses the whole usable roof. No new solar output or solar savings are given, and no extra array is planned on top of the existing one.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The city's solar-readiness record (Local Law 24) lists the roof as not solar ready, with no roof condition or roof age recorded, and lists installed solar of 228.2 kW, financed through a power purchase agreement. This differs from the 380 kW entered by the user. Please confirm which is correct and who owns the array.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Because the roof is listed as not solar ready and its age is unknown, the roof should be checked, and possibly repaired or replaced, before any roof work.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Scenario A, efficiency only: share of goal about 21% to 59% (6.2% to 17.6% cut in grid use). It does not reach the 30% goal.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario A upfront cost is typically $39,769 to $136,643; the median of similar NYC projects is about $87,016. With no incentive counted, net cost is the same.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario A simple payback is about 4.1 to 49.1 years (median case about 14 years). This is a simple payback, not the full SAM model.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario A is within budget: the cost is about 10% to 34% of the $400,000. Outage backup hours are zero; it adds no backup power.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario B (efficiency plus new solar within budget) and Scenario C (deep efficiency, whole-roof solar and battery) were not costed. No free roof exists for new solar, and the solar production data was not available. They can be compared if a verified free roof area is found. Rooftop solar alone would not reach the goal in any case.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: The budget is entered as a capital amount for 2027 and is treated as one total upfront figure.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Standard efficiency package: typical range $39,769 to $136,643; the median of similar NYC projects is about $87,016. Basis: about 33,991 kWh saved a year (middle of the 10-20% planning estimate) at $1.17 to $4.02 per kWh saved, the middle half of completed NYC public-sector lighting and comprehensive projects since 2016 (NYSERDA data). These are benchmarks, not quotes.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The efficiency savings percents are planning estimates, not backed by project data for this building.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Federal elective pay (direct payment for governmental entities) was open as of 2026-10-18, for solar placed in service by 2027-12-31. It applies to solar, and no new solar is planned. It is left out of net cost.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: NYSERDA NY-Sun commercial solar incentive: status uncertain, because the program dashboard could not be read automatically. Left out of net cost; check the dashboard in a browser if solar is revisited.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The NYC Solar Schools program (DCAS, NYPA, NYC Public Schools) puts rooftop solar on DOE schools under power purchase agreements. Whether this school is in its pipeline is not known. It is left out of net cost; ask DCAS or the SCA.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: None of the cost totals include replacing or repairing the roof. A roofer's quote is needed, since the roof is listed as not solar ready and its age is unknown.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 0, confirm data and budget: confirm the floor area, existing solar size and ownership (user entry, city record and city solar record disagree), lighting type, roof replacement year, the budget year and type, and the tariff on a Con Edison bill.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 1, professional reviews: a licensed structural PE or RA analysis and a roof condition survey before any roof or electrical work, including the existing array.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 2, efficiency measures: commission an energy audit and install the efficiency measures that fit the findings (lighting and controls first, unless already done). Then re-run the plan with the measured results to see how far the 30% goal is closed.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 3, permits and Con Edison: file Department of Buildings permits using a licensed electrician, get FDNY rooftop access review for any roof work, and ask Con Edison for an interconnection review if the existing array changes. Go through DCAS, NYC Public Schools or the SCA as the approval route.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 4, solar installation: not planned now because there is no free roof. Revisit only if an engineer verifies free roof area or the roof is replaced, and ask DCAS about the Solar Schools program.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 5, battery, commissioning and verification: check results against Con Edison bills each year. A battery is not sized; consider one once critical load kW and backup hours are given.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Scenario A gives no backup power. Outage hours are zero. Scenarios B and C were not modeled, so no outage hours for a battery are given. Solar panels shut off in an outage without a battery, so the existing array does not keep the school powered.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Critical loads named by the user are emergency lighting and communications. The critical load in kW and wanted backup hours were left blank, so no battery was sized.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The current FEMA flood map shows zone X, an area of minimal flood hazard. Only the flood zone was read: the 2015 preliminary map, and heat and winter-storm ratings, were not checked.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: A licensed PE or RA must do the structural analysis and a roof condition survey. The roof cannot be certified from these records.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Required for any electrical work: a licensed electrician, FDNY rooftop access review, and a Con Edison interconnection review if the existing solar changes. The Department of Buildings handles permits; the contact list at the end has the links.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: A major roof renovation on an existing building triggers the city's sustainable roof rules (Local Laws 92 and 94 of 2019): the roof must carry solar, a green roof, or both. Check this before replacing the roof.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The owner is the DOE, so approval runs through DCAS, NYC Public Schools or the SCA. The city's tax record shows no landmark flag, so no Landmarks review is indicated. No flood-zone review is indicated, as the zone is X.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

sections.title: Path to net-zero and learning resources

claims.text: Closing the 30% gap likely needs deeper efficiency (envelope, ventilation, cooling and controls), checked by an energy audit, plus confirming that the existing solar is counted correctly. Switching heating from gas to electric would raise electricity use and work against this goal, so it should be planned separately.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: The solar production call returned no data because the existing array already fills the usable roof. Missing: output and savings for any new solar, and scenarios B and C. Next step: have an engineer or roofer verify free roof area, then re-run.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Intake differences: floor area of 115,325 sq ft (user, and city energy report) against 135,600 sq ft (tax record); existing solar size of 380 kW (user) against 228.2 kW (city solar record); address 236th Street against 235th Street. The user's values are the working figures. Please confirm.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The price is the New York commercial average, not this building's own tariff. Several Con Edison general-service tariffs exist, and none is confirmed as this building's; confirm the tariff on a bill. Savings use the state average, so confidence is lower.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The incentives list is kept by a person and each official page is re-read by the system. NY-Sun and the Solar Schools program are uncertain and are left out of net cost.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Not provided in the intake: roof replacement year, roof condition, lighting type, heating fuel, cooling type, building controls, goal type, critical load kW, backup hours and electricity rate. Roof age and condition are also blank in the city record. Claims depending on them have lower confidence.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Scenario A is costed with no new solar. Efficiency savings percents are planning estimates and only 62% to 88% is counted. Confidence in the efficiency range is low, since payback ranges widely. Only the flood zone was read.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Savings cannot be assured. Every figure is an estimate with a range.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

roadmap.footer_note: All figures are planning estimates with ranges, not quotes. The roof cannot be certified from these records; a licensed PE or RA must do the structural analysis.
